newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No rigid 3.0 percent EMU deficit target - de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: No rigid 3.0 percent EMU deficit target - de Silguy.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday there was no question of the 3.0 percent deficit qualifying criteria for the single European currency being rigidly applied.
"There is no question of rigid application... of the 3.0 percent figure," de Silguy told a group of Italian reporters during a briefing on the economic situation in France.

"There is a small margin for interpretation, but we must not take any risks with the euro's credibility, which implies a strict implementation of the treaty conditions," his spokesman quoted him as having said.
Under the EU's Maastricht Treaty, members of the euro zone are supposed to limit government budget deficits to no more than 3.0 percent of GDP.
